findings.issue: `Function.Even.deriv` proves `Function.Odd (deriv f)`, but the `P.deriv` pattern upstream means "deriv preserves P" (`AnalyticAt.deriv : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (deriv f) x`, `AnalyticOnNhd.deriv` — both used in this PR), and in Mathlib's own `Function.Even`/`Odd` file a unary `Even.op` keeps evenness (`Even.const_smul : (r • g).Even`, `Even.add`, `Even.left_comp`) while any parity flip is spelled out in the name (`Even.mul_odd`, `Even.smul_odd`, `Odd.smul_even`). findings.issue: `namespace EpsilonEridani.Real` introduces a namespace layer no other file in the repo uses; the other Bessel family in the same tree is `EpsilonEridani.besselK (ν x : ℝ)` and the neighbours are `EpsilonEridani.gegenbauerThreeHalves`, `EpsilonEridani.Polynomial.legendre` (the latter nested only because its declarations are `Polynomial`s and gain dot notation). `Real` yields no dot notation for `(x : ℝ)` arguments, so the extra component only splits the API.

findings.evidence: Lines 92-97: "Here \"reduced\" means `j_l(x) / x ^ l`, not the Riccati–Bessel function `x * j_l(x)`"; no upstream declaration uses "reduced" for a spherical Bessel quantity (`grep -r 'phericalBessel' upstream/` → no matches).
findings.fix: Name it for what it is, e.g. `sphericalBesselJDivPow` (consistent with this PR's own `..._div_pow` vocabulary) or a `rayleigh`-based name, and rename the dependent lemmas.
findings.issue: `reducedSphericalBesselJ` names `j_l(x)/x^l` "reduced", a term neither A&S §10.1 nor DLMF §10.49 attaches to this quantity, while in scattering/nuclear usage "reduced" is the opposite factor (`x * j_l(x)`, the Riccati–Bessel function / reduced radial function). The docstring itself has to warn the reader off that reading — a name that needs a disclaimer against the expected meaning is misleading, and it propagates to ~12 public lemmas.

findings.issue: `tendsto_sphericalBesselJ_div_pow` omits the filter, so the name does not say where the limit is taken — and §0.3's remaining large-argument asymptotics will want exactly this unqualified name for an `atTop` statement. Upstream names the directly analogous lemma with the filter.

summary: Four naming issues: `Function.Even.deriv` reads as "deriv preserves evenness" but proves oddness; the new `EpsilonEridani.Real` namespace layer diverges from the repo's other special functions (`EpsilonEridani.besselK`); `reducedSphericalBesselJ` coins "reduced" in a sense its own docstring has to disclaim; and the limit lemma omits the filter that upstream and the adjacent repo file both put in the name.
